headline_marked: JetBrains [[launches ThinkRail, an agentic IDE]] built on git worktrees
headline: JetBrains launches ThinkRail, an agentic IDE built on git worktrees
summary: ThinkRail uses isolated Git worktrees for each workspace, allowing parallel agent execution and keeping the main branch clean. It's built spec-first, with agents reading and maintaining a connected graph of spec files.
details: ThinkRail, a new agentic IDE from JetBrains InnovationHub, is designed around the pi coding agent. It offers a rich UI while the pi agent handles models, skills, and session state in-process.

A core feature is its use of git worktrees for every workspace. This allows developers to cut isolated workspaces with their own branches, files, and terminals, ensuring the main branch remains clean.

The IDE is built spec-first, meaning projects include a connected graph of spec files alongside the code. The pi agent reads, searches, and maintains these specs, ensuring intent survives coding sessions.
ThinkRail integrates the VS Code editor engine, providing syntax highlighting, rendered markdown, and file tabs per workspace. It also features real PTYs scoped to each worktree for direct testing.

The platform allows real-time collaboration, enabling users to pair with an agent across Monaco tabs, terminals, and diffs. A live Git diff of the workspace branch helps review the agent's contributions.
ThinkRail is an Apache-2.0 licensed project from JetBrains InnovationHub. It requires Git and an authenticated pi provider, with a local launcher available for browser UI access.

headline_marked: New AI theory proposes [[Hybrid Cognitive Civilization and Artificial General Experience (AGE)]] beyond AGI
headline: New AI theory proposes Hybrid Cognitive Civilization and Artificial General Experience (AGE) beyond AGI
summary: A new perspective challenges the linear path to ASI, introducing Artificial General Experience (AGE) and envisioning a future where human and AI cognition form a complementary, hybrid civilization.
details: A new theory challenges the traditional linear model of AI development, moving beyond the idea of AGI as a mere stepping stone to Artificial Superintelligence (ASI). It introduces the concept of Artificial General Experience (AGE), which incorporates dimensions of time, context, and memory into AI evaluation.

The author highlights fundamental differences between human biological cognition, rooted in evolution and homeostasis, and the mathematical-computational nature of AI. This distinction suggests that direct homology between their mechanisms may not be the most productive analytical approach.

Instead of seeking to replicate human cognition, the focus shifts to the functional complementarity of human and AI systems. This perspective suggests that AI's evolution is multidimensional, aiming not to replace humans but to integrate with them.

This integration is envisioned as the emergence of a hybrid cognitive civilization. Key considerations for this future include the interoperability of diverse thought infrastructures and the preservation of individual cognitive sovereignty.
